answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake reclaimable only after a period of honest activity. Picture the network as a graph where each identity is a vertex: an attacker wanting many vertices must lock capital behind every one, so fake identities become expensive instead of free. Like shale, which forms only slowly in layers under pressure, reputation should build gradually, not appear overnight. As a raven once carried messages only between trusted roosts, attestations from long-standing participants should outweigh new accounts' endorsements, so a sybil swarm cannot vouch itself in.
